info.title: Assinafy API Reference
info.description:
The **Assinafy API** is RESTful and gives access to documents, users, workspaces and signers, authenticated with an API key or an access token. ## REST API HTTP verbs are used according to the request type: - `GET` to retrieve data; - `POST` to create; - `PUT` to update; - `DELETE` to remove. ### Content type The default request and response format is JSON. ### HTTPS and TLS All requests must use HTTPS with **TLS 1.2 or higher**. Connections using TLS 1.0 or 1.1 are rejected during the handshake, before any HTTP response is sent, so they fail with a connection error rather than an HTTP status code. If your client reports errors such as `unsupported protocol` or `Could not create SSL/TLS secure channel`, update its runtime or HTTP library, or enable TLS 1.2 explicitly (older Java and .NET Framework versions may need this). ### Response envelope Every response is wrapped as `{ status, message, data }`. `status` mirrors the HTTP status code (`200` means success); `data` holds the payload on success and is `null` on error. ### Authentication Most endpoints require authentication. There are two options: a fixed **API key** (`X-Api-Key` header) or an **access token** (`Authorization: Bearer ...`). See the Authentication section for details. Applications that act in *other people's* workspaces use OAuth instead — see **OAuth Integration Guide**. ## Searching, paginating and sorting List endpoints accept these query parameters: | Parameter | Description | |-----------|-------------| | `search` | Search term. | | `page` | Page number. | | `per-page`| Records per page (max 100). | | `sort` | Sort order, e.g. `name` or `-created_at`. | …and return pagination metadata in response headers: `X-Pagination-Current-Page`, `X-Pagination-Total-Count`, `X-Pagination-Page-Count`, `X-Pagination-Per-Page`. ## Rate limits Requests are limited per minute: per user when authenticated, and per IP address otherwise. A few sensitive endpoints (payments, coupons, MFA, OAuth) have tighter limits of their own. Every limited response carries: | Header | Description | |--------|-------------| | `X-Rate-Limit-Limit` | Requests allowed in the current window. | | `X-Rate-Limit-Remaining` | Requests left in the current window. | | `X-Rate-Limit-Reset` | Seconds until the window resets. | Past the limit the API answers `429 Too Many Requests` with a `Retry-After` header (seconds). Wait that long before retrying. ## Test and production environments During development use the **sandbox**:
API: https://sandbox.assinafy.com.br/v1 · APP: https://app-sandbox.assinafy.com.br When ready, switch to **production**:
API: https://api.assinafy.com.br/v1 · APP: https://app.assinafy.com.br ## Error codes The error code is returned in the `status` attribute. | Code | Type | |------|------| | 400 | Bad Request | | 401 | Unauthorized | | 403 | Forbidden | | 404 | Not Found | | 415 | Unsupported Media Type | | 429 | Too Many Requests | | 500 | Internal Server Error | ## Client libraries and tools Official SDKs for eight languages, a CLI, an MCP server and an n8n node are listed under **SDKs & Tools**. To work from the spec directly — Postman, Insomnia or your own generated client — see **OpenAPI & API Clients**.

post.description:
Request signatures on a document. Use `method: virtual` to sign without input fields, or `method: collect` to place input fields on specific pages.

**Digital certificate signing works only on `virtual` assignments.** A `DigitalCertificate` signer cannot sign placed fields, so a `collect` assignment with one is refused with `400` before anything is charged.

For **virtual**, the document may be in `uploaded`, `metadata_processing` or `metadata_ready`; it is promoted to `pending_signature` automatically once metadata processing completes. For **collect**, the document must be in `metadata_ready` (fields reference specific pages).

`step` controls signing order: signers sharing a step sign in parallel, and the next step is notified only after the previous step completes. If supplied, every signer must supply it and values must be contiguous starting at 1.

[Copy as Markdown](https://api.assinafy.com.br/v1/docs/markdown?method=post&path=%2Fv1%2Fdocuments%2F%7BdocumentId%7D%2Fassignments) [Open in ChatGPT](https://chatgpt.com/?q=Read%20the%20API%20documentation%20at%20https%3A%2F%2Fapi.assinafy.com.br%2Fv1%2Fdocs%2Fmarkdown%3Fmethod%3Dpost%26path%3D%252Fv1%252Fdocuments%252F%257BdocumentId%257D%252Fassignments%20and%20help%20me%20integrate%20this%20endpoint.) [Open in Claude](https://claude.ai/new?q=Read%20the%20API%20documentation%20at%20https%3A%2F%2Fapi.assinafy.com.br%2Fv1%2Fdocs%2Fmarkdown%3Fmethod%3Dpost%26path%3D%252Fv1%252Fdocuments%252F%257BdocumentId%257D%252Fassignments%20and%20help%20me%20integrate%20this%20endpoint.)

method.description: `virtual` signs without input fields; `collect` places input fields on pages. Signers with `DigitalCertificate` verification need `virtual` (`collect` returns `400`).

verification_method.description: How the signer's identity is verified before signing. `Email` (default) sends a one-time code to the signer's email; `Whatsapp` sends the code over WhatsApp — the verification itself is not billed, but it requires the WhatsApp notification channel, so the signer costs 0.45 credits (available only on paid subscriptions); `DigitalCertificate` has the signer sign with their own ICP-Brasil certificate (A1/A3) — it requires the Digital Certificate feature, the signer must have a CPF or CNPJ in `government_id`, must be alone in its signing step, needs `method: virtual` (a `collect` assignment with a `DigitalCertificate` signer returns `400`), and is charged 0.5 credits per signer. A CPF requires that person's certificate (an e-CPF, or an e-CNPJ naming them as legal representative); a CNPJ requires an e-CNPJ for that company, from any of its representatives. `IdDocumentFaceMatchBasic` verifies the signer from a photo of their government ID, a photo of them holding it and a liveness check — it requires the ID Document + Face Match feature, the signer must have a valid CPF in `government_id`, and is charged a per-signer fee. Omit to default to `Email`.

notification_methods.description: How the signer is told a signature is being requested. **Exactly one method per signer** — the array shape is historical, and sending two returns `400`. The method must also be compatible with `verification_method`: `Email` verification takes `Email`, `Whatsapp` verification takes `Whatsapp`, and `DigitalCertificate` and `IdDocumentFaceMatchBasic` take either. WhatsApp incurs an additional cost and is available only on paid subscriptions. Omit it to have it inferred from `verification_method`, or `{"Email"}` when neither is sent. See **Verification & Notification Methods** for the full pairing table.

entries.description: Required for `collect`: field placements per page. In `collect`, every signer listed in `signers` must appear once and own at least one field here; otherwise `400`.

message.description: Text included in the invitation email.

expires_at.description: ISO 8601; default is no expiration. Must be at least one hour in the future. A UTC offset in the value is honored (`2026-12-31T23:59:59-03:00` is `2027-01-01T02:59:59Z`); a value without one is read as UTC, and a date alone (`2026-12-31`) means 23:59 UTC that day.

copy_receivers.description: Signer IDs that only receive a copy.

post.description:
Estimate the cost of creating an assignment without creating it, returning a cost breakdown and the current account balances. Signer IDs are not required — only the verification/notification method affects cost. Each assignment consumes 1 document from the plan allowance; if exhausted, an extra document is charged from credits (`needs_extra_document` = true). `blocking_reason` may be `PendingPayment`, `InsufficientDocuments` or `InsufficientCredits`.

### Pricing

Per-unit costs (in credits) used to build the estimate:

| Item | Cost |
|------|------|
| Extra document | 1 credit |
| Email notification | 0 credits |
| WhatsApp notification | 0.45 credits |
| Digital certificate signature (per signer) | 0.5 credits |
| Identity document verification (per signer) | depends on the plan, see the table below |

| Plan | Price per signer |
|------|------------------|
| Free | 1.5 credits |
| Standard | 1 credit |
| Pro | 0.5 credits |
| Other plans and enterprise contracts | 0.25 credits |

`Email` and `Whatsapp` verification are not priced separately — their only line in the `breakdown` is their notification. A `Whatsapp`-verified signer therefore shows up as a WhatsApp notification, because that channel is mandatory for that verification method. A `DigitalCertificate` signer adds the digital-certificate signature cost **on top of** its notification cost; it appears in the `breakdown` under the `SignatureDigitalCertificate` code. An `IdDocumentFaceMatchBasic` signer likewise adds your plan's verification price on top of its notification, under the `VerificationIdDocumentFaceMatchBasic` code.

[Copy as Markdown](https://api.assinafy.com.br/v1/docs/markdown?method=post&path=%2Fv1%2Fdocuments%2F%7BdocumentId%7D%2Fassignments%2Festimate-cost) [Open in ChatGPT](https://chatgpt.com/?q=Read%20the%20API%20documentation%20at%20https%3A%2F%2Fapi.assinafy.com.br%2Fv1%2Fdocs%2Fmarkdown%3Fmethod%3Dpost%26path%3D%252Fv1%252Fdocuments%252F%257BdocumentId%257D%252Fassignments%252Festimate-cost%20and%20help%20me%20integrate%20this%20endpoint.) method.description: Send the method you will create the assignment with. With `collect`, a `DigitalCertificate` signer returns `400`, because certificate signing works only on `virtual` assignments.

signers.description: Required for `virtual`; each entry may be `{}` to default to Email.

verification_method.description: Verification method to price. `Whatsapp` forces the WhatsApp notification, so it prices at 0.45 credits per signer; `DigitalCertificate` adds the per-signer signature cost on top of its notification, and with `method: collect` returns `400` (certificate signers sign only virtual assignments). `IdDocumentFaceMatchBasic` requires its account feature, requires the signer to have a valid CPF in `government_id`, and is charged your plan's per-signer verification price on top of its notification.

notification_methods.description: The notification channel to price — exactly one per signer, subject to the same pairing rules as **Create assignment**. `Whatsapp` costs 0.45 credits per signer. Omit it to have it inferred from `verification_method`.

put.description:
Creates the document's contract terms, or changes only the attributes sent (see the request body for what `null` does). `external_references`, when sent, replaces the whole list. Records a `document_contract_updated` event when the terms change; a retry that changes nothing records none. The body must be a JSON object with at least one attribute. With `parent_document_id`, the document is instead linked as an amendment, renewal or termination of that contract (or of any document in its family, resolved to the root) and the other attributes are the terms it changes; a later `PUT` on a pending amendment merges into that delta (a `null` drops a key) and `parent_document_id: null` unlinks it; every change to the link records `document_contract_amendment_updated` on this document. The delta applies to the parent once the document is certificated (at once, if it already is), in signing order (the order the documents' certifications were recorded in, fixed for each once it is; a certificated document with none recorded waits, and is placed by its certification time an hour on): instruments signed earlier apply first, one that cannot holds the later ones back, and an instrument signed before one already applied is blocked instead of applied over it. Applying records `document_contract_amended`; an applied amendment is read-only. A cancelled, declined or expired document takes no new terms and no new link; terms or a link already on one stay and can still change. Send the `updated_at` you read with the write to have it refused (`409`) if the contract or link changed meanwhile. Needs a plan with contract tracking (`403` otherwise).

Reopens an expired contract; a terminated one returns `400`. Steps `term`, so the lifecycle alerts run again for the new term. Records a `document_contract_renewed` event. Needs a plan with contract tracking (`403` otherwise). The body names the `term` the renewal starts from (the contract's current one) or the `end_date` it renews to, so a renewal answered with a `5xx` error, or whose answer was lost, is safe to send again: the repeat is refused with `400`, as the contract is then in its next term and that date is no longer after the current one (or with `409`, when it sends the `updated_at` it read).

post.summary: Exchange a code, refresh token, or subject token for an access token
post.description:
Implements the RFC 6749 §5.1/§5.2 token-endpoint body contract in
     *         both directions: a successful exchange returns a flat JSON object with
     *         `access_token` at the top level, and a failure returns a flat
     *         `{error, error_description}` object — neither is wrapped in this API's
     *         usual response envelope, since no standard OAuth client library (or MCP
     *         connector) would find `access_token` or `error` inside a `data` key.
     *
     *         The third grant, `urn:ietf:params:oauth:grant-type:token-exchange` (RFC 8693),
     *         is restricted to a confidential internal-service client (see `/oauth/introspect`)
     *         and trades a front-end resource's access token (the `subject_token`) for one
     *         minted for THIS API — the crossing an MCP server makes after a user consents,
     *         since its own token can never be forwarded here directly. The issued token is
     *         never wider than the subject: `scope`, when sent, must be a subset of the
     *         subject's own scopes, and `resource` must equal this API's own resource
     *         identifier exactly. No refresh token is issued; the caller re-exchanges from
     *         the user's own token instead of holding unattended API access.

issued_token_type.description: Present only for the token-exchange grant, per RFC 8693 §2.2.1.

expires_in.description: For the token-exchange grant, clamped to the subject token's own remaining lifetime as well as the exchanged-token TTL — never longer than either.

refresh_token.description: Present only when the `offline_access` scope was requested AND consented on the authorization_code/refresh_token grants. Never present for the token-exchange grant. Without it a client must send the user through the authorization flow again once the access token expires.

scope.description: The scope of the ACCESS token. `offline_access` is a request-time signal rather than a permission, so it never appears here even when it was requested.

id_token.description: A signed OIDC id_token (RS256). Present only when the openid scope was granted.

400.description: `invalid_grant` (bad, expired, replayed, or wrong-client authorization code; a `code_verifier` outside the RFC 7636 grammar of 43-128 unreserved characters; redirect_uri mismatch; a refresh token whose authorization no longer includes `offline_access`; for token-exchange, a `subject_token` that is unusable, itself an exchanged token, not visible to service clients, or expired), `invalid_target` (a `resource` this server does not issue tokens for, one disagreeing with the authorized value, or — for token-exchange — one other than this API's own resource identifier), `invalid_scope` (token-exchange only: the requested `scope` is not a subset of the subject token's own scopes), `invalid_request` (token-exchange only: an unsupported `subject_token_type`/`requested_token_type`), or `unsupported_grant_type`

401.description: `invalid_client` — unknown/disabled client or failed client authentication. The description never reveals whether client_id exists.

429.description: Rate limit exceeded; wait the `Retry-After` seconds. Limited per caller IP.

Current state of the signer's identity document verification. Backfills a pending decision from the provider. Uses the signer access code.

**One live session per signer:** `can_start` is true before a provider session exists, and again once that session is Expired -- the capture link lapsed before anything was submitted, so the signer may open a new one. Once a session is Pending, In Review, Approved, Declined or Abandoned it is false. A signer who reaches Declined or Abandoned cannot restart here; the account must start a whole new process (new document, new assignment).

**In review:** the signer continues -- views, confirms their data and signs -- while the account reviews the result. The document is certificated only after the account approves every signer under review; if it rejects one, the document is cancelled and every signer receives the cancellation notice.

get.description:
Retrieve the document a signer has been invited to sign, using the signer access code. Marks the document as viewed. The assignment carries only this signer's items, and leaves out the other signers, their signing links (`signing_urls`), the copy receivers and the signing `summary`. The response adds `current_signer`: this signer, with their `verification_method`, `notification_methods` and `completed` (whether they have already signed). Returns 409 while the document is still being prepared (retry with backoff).

**Signers whose verification method is `DigitalCertificate`** must have confirmed their data *and* accepted the terms before this returns the document; otherwise it is `400`. Both are satisfied in one call to `PUT /v1/documents/{documentId}/signers/confirm-data` with `has_accepted_terms: true`, so send that before this endpoint — the `has_accepted_terms` query parameter here is too late to open the gate. `PUT /v1/signers/accept-terms` also works and is never gated.

post.description:
Generate a new document from a template. The request is checked (roles, fields, balance) before it returns, but the assignment is created in the background, so the response has `status: uploaded` and `assignment: null`. Follow the outcome on `GET /v1/documents/{documentId}` or through webhooks: when the send succeeds the status moves to `pending_signature` and `assignment_created` is sent; when it fails the status becomes `failed`, `document_processing_failed` is sent with the reason, and nothing is charged. When the template has fields, every signing role used must have at least one field; otherwise `400`. A template with placed signer fields sends a `collect` assignment, so it cannot take a `DigitalCertificate` signer (`400`); certificate signing needs a template without placed signer fields. Provide one signer entry per template role. An entry with `id` uses that existing signer; an entry with `email` reuses the account's signer with that email or creates one.

[Copy as Markdown](https://api.assinafy.com.br/v1/docs/markdown?method=post&path=%2Fv1%2Faccounts%2F%7BaccountId%7D%2Ftemplates%2F%7BtemplateId%7D%2Fdocuments) [Open in ChatGPT](https://chatgpt.com/?q=Read%20the%20API%20documentation%20at%20https%3A%2F%2Fapi.assinafy.com.br%2Fv1%2Fdocs%2Fmarkdown%3Fmethod%3Dpost%26path%3D%252Fv1%252Faccounts%252F%257BaccountId%257D%252Ftemplates%252F%257BtemplateId%257D%252Fdocuments%20and%20help%20me%20integrate%20this%20endpoint.) [Open in Claude](https://claude.ai/new?q=Read%20the%20API%20documentation%20at%20https%3A%2F%2Fapi.assinafy.com.br%2Fv1%2Fdocs%2Fmarkdown%3Fmethod%3Dpost%26path%3D%252Fv1%252Faccounts%252F%257BaccountId%257D%252Ftemplates%252F%257BtemplateId%257D%252Fdocuments%20and%20help%20me%20integrate%20this%20endpoint.)

role_id.description: The template role ID associated with the signer.

id.description: An existing signer's ID. Send either `id` or `email`; `id` wins when both are sent, and an unknown `id` returns `400`.

email.description: Used when `id` is not sent: the account's signer with this email is reused, or a new one is created with `name`.

name.description: Full name for a signer created from `email`.

whatsapp_phone_number.description: WhatsApp number for a signer created from `email`.

verification_method.description: Verification method for this signer. If provided without notification_methods, the notification method is inferred. Defaults to Email. `DigitalCertificate` has the signer sign with their own ICP-Brasil certificate — it requires the Digital Certificate feature, the signer must have a CPF or CNPJ in `government_id` (a CPF requires that person's certificate; a CNPJ requires an e-CNPJ for that company), must be alone in its signing step, and is charged 0.5 credits per signer. It is refused with `400` when the template has placed signer fields, because certificate signers sign only virtual assignments. `IdDocumentFaceMatchBasic` verifies the signer from a photo of their government ID, a photo of them holding it and a liveness check — it requires the ID Document + Face Match feature, the signer must have a valid CPF in `government_id`, and is charged a per-signer fee. Only applies to signers (not copy receivers).

notification_methods.description: Notification method codes for this signer. If provided without verification_method, the verification method is inferred. Defaults to Email. Only one method allowed per signer.

step.description: Positive integer that controls signing order. Signers sharing the same step sign in parallel; a step activates only after every signer in the previous step has signed. If supplied for any role it must be supplied for all, forming a contiguous sequence starting at 1. Copy receivers ignore this field.

editor_fields.description: Values for the fields placed on the template's `Editor` role, baked into the generated document. The `Editor` role takes no `signers` entry: it is filled only through this list. Every field placed on it needs an entry with a non-empty `value` (`400` otherwise); when it has no fields, send nothing. In `signers`, every `Signer` role needs an entry (`400` otherwise), and a `CopyReceiver` role takes an entry only for someone who should receive the certified document; a copy receiver's `verification_method`, `notification_methods` and `step` are ignored.

field_id.description: The field identifier, matching the field_id in the template data.

value.description: The value to assign to the field.

name.description: Title for the document. Defaults to the template name.

expires_at.description: Assignment expiration date (ISO 8601). No expiration by default. Must be at least one hour in the future. A UTC offset in the value is honored (`2026-12-31T23:59:59-03:00` is `2027-01-01T02:59:59Z`); a value without one is read as UTC, and a date alone (`2026-12-31`) means 23:59 UTC that day.

tags.description: Tag names to attach to the new document. Names that don't exist are auto-created. The template's default-document-tags are always applied; values here are merged on top (duplicates removed).

DisplaySettings.description: A field placement rectangle on a document page. Geometry values are pixels in Assinafy's 150-DPI page image, measured from the upper-left corner. Clients must keep the rectangle within the selected page's width and height; the API does not clamp out-of-bounds values.

Document.description: A document and its current lifecycle state.

artifacts.description: Artifact download URLs keyed by name. Always `original`, plus `thumbnail` once one exists. A certificated document also carries `certificated`, `certificate-page` and `bundle`, and `pades` when it was signed with a digital certificate — the PAdES version holds the signers' ICP-Brasil signatures, which certification flattens out of the certificated PDF.

verification_code.description: The code printed on the certificate page. Anyone can check it with `GET /v1/documents/{verification_code}/verify` or on `verification_url`. `null` until the document is `certificated`, and on documents certificated before verification codes existed.

verification_url.description: The public verification page for this document. `null` until the document is `certificated`.

assignment.description: The document's assignment, or `null` before one is created. The server decides when it is included, whatever `expand` the request sends: the document list, `GET /v1/documents/{documentId}`, the signer's document list and document creation from a template always include it; `/documents/search` and the upload response never do. Only the rename response follows `?expand=assignment`.

pages.description: The document's pages. Included on the same responses as `assignment`, and also on the upload response.

has_contract.description: Only on `GET /v1/documents/{documentId}` read by the workspace, while the environment has contract tracking on: not with a signer's access code, not in document lists or webhooks, and left out when the lookup fails, so a missing key means unknown. Whether `GET /v1/accounts/{accountId}/documents/{documentId}/contract` answers with contract terms, the document's own or those of a contract it amends whose document still exists, so a page can lay out the contract section before reading it.

limits.description: Limits of the workspace's current plan. Returned only by `GET /v1/accounts/{accountId}`, not in account lists. More keys may be added.

webhook_endpoints.description: How many webhook endpoints the workspace can have: `1`, or `3` with the Multiple Webhooks feature. Creating one past the limit returns `403`.

Tag.description: A workspace-scoped label. Names are unique per workspace (case-insensitive).

DocumentContract.description: The contract terms tracked on a document.

currency.description: ISO 4217 code; `BRL` when a value is sent without one.

term.description: Steps on every renewal, starting at 1.

owner_id.description: ID of the workspace member who owns the contract. When the owner is no longer a member of the workspace (removed, left, or deleted with their account), the hourly run hands the contract to the first owner who is still an active member, or leaves it without one; an inactive member stays the owner. The contract's e-mails (renewal notice, expiring, expired, renewed) go to the first of the owner and the document's creator who is an active member, as that member's notification preferences allow.

metadata.description: Up to 50 keys of your own, each holding text of at most 500 characters; `null` when there are none. A key ending in `_at` cannot hold a number: the API returns numbers under such keys as dates.

external_references.description: IDs outside systems use for this contract, ordered by system and id.

document.description: Only with `expand=document`: the document the terms are tracked on.

amendments.description: Only on the single-contract read: the documents that amend, renew or terminate this contract, the applied ones first by `number`, then the pending ones.

DocumentContractInput.description: Every attribute is optional and only the ones sent change. `null` clears an attribute, except `auto_renew` (back to `false`) and `currency` (back to `BRL` while a `value` is set); `status` does not accept `null`. A changed `end_date` starts a new `term`.

status.description: On creation any status, so a contract that ended before it was tracked is registered as it ended: `expired` needs an `end_date` in the past, `terminated` its `end_date`; neither is walked by the lifecycle. Afterwards only `draft` or `active` (a contract in force never goes back to `draft`): `expired` and `terminated` are set by the lifecycle and the terminate endpoint; a closed contract is reopened by renewing it.

counterparty_name.description: Emoji are kept; other characters outside the 3-byte range are dropped.

counterparty_taxpayer_id.description: A valid CPF or CNPJ, formatted or not.

currency.description: Three letters, such as `BRL` or `USD`, stored in capitals; `BRL` when a `value` is set without one.

auto_renew.description: Whether the hourly run starts the next term the day after `end_date`, by `renewal_term_months`, instead of expiring the contract.

renewal_term_months.description: How far a renewal by the term moves `end_date`; 12 when unset.

notice_period_days.description: Days before `end_date` the notice period starts (`document_contract_renewal_notice`); none when unset.

owner_id.description: An active member of this workspace.

metadata.description: Your own fields: up to 50 keys of 1 to 40 letters, digits, `_`, `-` or `.`, each holding plain text of at most 500 characters; no number under a key ending in `_at`, or `stuck_since`.

external_references.description: Replaces the whole list; `[]` or `null` clears it. Two items whose `system` and `id` compare equal case aside are one reference (the first sent is kept); a pair the database takes for one beyond that (accents, `ß` and `ss`) answers `400`.

system.description: Letters, digits, `_`, `-` and `.`; stored in lower case.

id.description: Kept as sent; must not contain emoji or other 4-byte characters.

parent_document_id.description: Links the document as an amendment of this contract document, or of any document in its family (resolved to the root); `null` unlinks a pending amendment. With it, the other attributes are the terms the instrument changes, not terms of its own; on a pending amendment a `null` value drops that term from the delta rather than clearing it on the parent.

relation_type.description: Required on the first link. `amendment` may change `value`, `currency`, `start_date` (effective from, display only), `end_date`, `auto_renew`, `renewal_term_months`, `notice_period_days`, `counterparty_name`, `counterparty_taxpayer_id` and `metadata`; `renewal` only `end_date` and `value`; `termination` only `end_date` (the effective date).

updated_at.description: Optional precondition: the `updated_at` the client read the contract (or this document's amendment link) with, as the API returned it. If the contract or link changed since, nothing is written and the answer is `409` with `code: ContractChanged`. Not sent, or `null`: the write applies whatever changed meanwhile (last write wins). Compared to the second; a fraction of a second, as a JavaScript date prints it, is read and ignored. New terms and a first link have nothing to have read, so sending one answers `409`; on a pending amendment, send the link's own `updated_at` (the GET on that document).

DocumentContractAmendment.description: A document that amends, renews or terminates a contract: its link and the terms it changes. The parent's terms take the delta once this document is certificated; until then the parent is untouched.

document_name.example: Aditivo 1 - Contrato de prestação de serviços.pdf

parent_document_id.description: The contract document whose terms change.

number.description: Position among the parent's applied amendments by signing date; `null` while pending.

status.description: `applied` once the delta moved the parent's terms.

apply_error.description: Why a signed instrument has not applied yet, retried every hour: the workspace's plan does not include contract tracking (it applies on the first run after the plan returns), the parent would not take the delta, an instrument signed before this one has not applied yet, one signed after it has already applied (this one then stays blocked: unlink it, and record what it still changes on a new instrument), or an unexpected failure.

terms.description: The delta: only the terms this instrument changes; `null` when it changes none (a termination on the day it is signed).

changes.description: Every parent field the roll-up moves, as `{from, to}`: a preview while pending, the record once applied; `null` when it moves none.

ContractInputError.description:
The request breaks a contract rule. `errors` has one entry per problem found: the `field` as sent (`null` when the request as a whole is refused), a stable `code` to translate, and the `message` in the platform's language; `message` at the top is the first entry's. The contract's own rules on the terms, and the external references' items, report every field that breaks one, an entry per field (its first problem); the other checks (the body, its fields, the contract's state, a renewal's or a link's conditions) stop at the first problem they find.

| Code | Field | Refused when |
|------|-------|--------------|
| `InvalidBody` | — | The body is not a JSON object (a list, a bare value), or a `PUT` of contract terms sends no attribute. |
| `UnknownField` | the attribute | The endpoint does not take the attribute; one entry per attribute. |
| `NotSingleValue` | the attribute | On a `PUT` of contract terms, a list sent for a term that takes one value (every term but `metadata` and `external_references`). On a link, the same list answers the term's own code. |
| `Required` | `parent_document_id`, `relation_type`, `external_references[i].system`, `external_references[i].id` | A first link without `parent_document_id` (a pending link that was removed meanwhile) or `relation_type`; an `external_references` item without `system` or `id` (`i` is its place in the list sent, from 0). |
| `Invalid` | the field | The value is not of the field's type or form: `status` not one of the four; `currency` not three letters; `auto_renew` not a boolean; `owner_id` not a user id; `value` not a number; `counterparty_name` holding HTML; `metadata` not an object; `external_references` not a list, an item's `system` (`external_references[i].system`) with characters other than letters, digits, `_`, `-` and `.`, or its `id` (`external_references[i].id`) with an emoji or another 4-byte character; `parent_document_id` not text; `relation_type` not `amendment`, `renewal` or `termination`; `term` not a whole number from 1; `reason` not text. On the list: a filter sent as a list, a `status` not one of the four, `ending_within_days` not a whole number. |
| `TooSmall`, `TooBig` | the field | `value` below 0 or above 9999999999999.99; `renewal_term_months` outside 1 to 600; `notice_period_days` (and the list's `ending_within_days`) outside 0 to 3650. |
| `TooLong` | the field | `counterparty_name` over 255 characters, counting each emoji as stored (several characters); `counterparty_taxpayer_id` over 20; `reason` over 500; `external_references[i].system` over 64 or `external_references[i].id` over 255. |
| `TooMany` | `external_references` | More than 20 items. |
| `TooManyDecimals` | `value` | More than two decimal places. |
| `InvalidDate` | `start_date`, `end_date`, `updated_at`; the list's `end_date_from`, `end_date_to` | Not a date as `YYYY-MM-DD` (an impossible one such as `2026-02-30` included); `updated_at` not a date and time as the API writes it (`2026-10-23T12:00:00Z`, or with an offset). |
| `DateTooEarly` | `start_date`, `end_date` | Before the year 1000. |
| `DateTooLate` | `end_date` | A renewal by the term would pass 9999-12-31. |
| `EndBeforeStart` | `end_date` | Before `start_date`. |
| `InvalidTaxpayerId` | `counterparty_taxpayer_id` | Not a valid CPF or CNPJ (formatted or not). |
| `NotAMember` | `owner_id` | Not an active member of the workspace. |
| `TooManyKeys` | `metadata` | More than 50 keys. |
| `InvalidKey` | `metadata` | A key that is not 1 to 40 letters, digits, `_`, `-` or `.`. |
| `InvalidValue` | `metadata` | A value that is not plain text of at most 500 characters. |
| `NumberUnderDateKey` | `metadata` | A number under a key ending in `_at`, or `stuck_since`, which the API would return as a date. |
| `ListKeys` | `metadata` | Keys `0`, `1`, `2`…, which would read back as a list. |
| `DuplicateReference` | `external_references` | Two items the database takes for one (accents, `ß` and `ss`); items equal case aside are merged, not refused. |
| `StatusNotSettable` | `status` | A tracked contract sent `expired` or `terminated`, or a closed one sent `draft` or `active`: a contract is closed by terminating it and reopened by renewing it. |
| `CannotReturnToDraft` | `status` | An `active` contract sent `draft`. |
| `ExpiredNeedsPastEndDate` | `end_date` | New terms with status `expired` and no `end_date` before today. |
| `TerminatedNeedsEndDate` | `end_date` | New terms with status `terminated` and no `end_date`. |
| `UnsignableDocument` | — | New terms, or a first link, on a cancelled, declined or expired document. Terms or a link already on one stay editable. |
| `DocumentIsAmendment` | — | Terms of its own for a document linked as an amendment: its terms are the changes it makes. |
| `DocumentHasOwnTerms` | — | A link for a document that tracks a contract of its own: a document is a contract or an amendment, never both. |
| `ParentHasNoTerms` | `parent_document_id` | The parent named has no contract terms, nor amends a contract that has. |
| `ParentTerminated` | `parent_document_id` | The parent contract is terminated. |
| `NoTermChanged` | — | An `amendment` that changes no term, also by dropping its last one. A `renewal` or `termination` may change none. |
| `TermNotAllowed` | the term | A term the relation type cannot change: a `renewal` changes only `end_date` and `value`, a `termination` only `end_date`. |
| `AmendmentApplied` | — | The amendment applied when its document was signed and can no longer change. |
| `TermOrEndDateRequired` | — | A renewal sends neither `term` nor `end_date`. |
| `TermMismatch` | `term` | Not the contract's current term: the renewal already happened. |
| `ContractTerminated` | — | A renewal of a terminated contract. |
| `EndDateRequired` | `end_date` | A renewal by the term, or a `renewal` link without `end_date`, of a contract without an end date. |
| `EndDateNotAfterCurrent` | `end_date` | A renewal, or a `renewal` link, to a date not after the current end date. |
| `AlreadyTerminated` | — | A termination of a contract already terminated. |

A body that is not valid JSON is refused before it reaches these endpoints, with the platform's `400` and no `errors`. A link is also checked against what applying it today would give the parent, so a delta the contract would refuse comes back with the contract's own codes.

tags.name: Quick Start
tags.description:
Steps to quickly start using the API. By the end you'll be able to create a document and invite signers.

### 1. Create a user account

During development, create a user account in the **sandbox** (https://app-sandbox.assinafy.com.br). For integrations using an API key, create a *separate* user account (e.g. *My App*) so you can grant it only the access it needs. Use the production app (https://app.assinafy.com.br) once you go live.

### 2. Set up credentials

Generate an **API key** from the *My Account → API* page in the Assinafy app, and note your **workspace account ID** from *My Account → Workspaces*. Use the API key only from a back-end system — never store it in client-side code.

For sandbox plan/credit purchases, use the test card `5510 3647 0363 3414`.

### 3. Upload a document

```shell
curl -X POST "https://api.assinafy.com.br/v1/accounts/{account_id}/documents" \
  -H 'X-Api-Key: {api_key}' \
  -F 'file=@/tmp/document.pdf'
```

Save the returned document `id` for the next steps.

### 4. Create signers

```shell
curl -X POST "https://api.assinafy.com.br/v1/accounts/{account_id}/signers" \
  -H 'X-Api-Key: {api_key}' \
  -H 'Content-Type: application/json' \
  -d '{ "full_name": "John Dove", "email": "john@example.com" }'
```

Save each signer `id`.

### 5. Request signatures

```shell
curl -X POST "https://api.assinafy.com.br/v1/documents/{document_id}/assignments" \
  -H 'X-Api-Key: {api_key}' \
  -H 'Content-Type: application/json' \
  -d '{ "method": "virtual", "signers": [{ "id": "{signer_id}" }] }'
```

The `virtual` method requires no input from the signer. To collect input fields, use the `collect` method — see the Assignment section.

tags.name: SDKs & Tools
tags.description:
Official client libraries, a command-line tool, an MCP server and an n8n node — all built against the same OpenAPI document that generates this reference. Source for everything lives at [github.com/assinafy](https://github.com/assinafy).

Every SDK exposes the same operations and reads the same credentials:

| Variable | Meaning |
|----------|---------|
| `ASSINAFY_API_KEY` | API key, sent as the `X-Api-Key` header. Create it from *My Account → API*. |
| `ASSINAFY_ACCOUNT_ID` | Workspace account id, from *My Account → Workspaces*. |
| `ASSINAFY_BASE_URL` | `https://sandbox.assinafy.com.br/v1` while developing, `https://api.assinafy.com.br/v1` in production. |

An API key is a long-lived secret with full workspace access. Use it only from a back-end system — never in a browser bundle or a shipped mobile app.

## Server-side SDKs

| Language | Package | Install | Source |
|----------|---------|---------|--------|
| TypeScript / Node | `@assinafy/sdk` | `npm install @assinafy/sdk` | [typescript-sdk](https://github.com/assinafy/typescript-sdk) |
| Python | `assinafy` | `pip install assinafy` | [python-sdk](https://github.com/assinafy/python-sdk) |
| Ruby | `assinafy` | `gem "assinafy"` | [ruby-sdk](https://github.com/assinafy/ruby-sdk) |
| Go | `github.com/assinafy/golang-sdk` | `go get github.com/assinafy/golang-sdk` | [golang-sdk](https://github.com/assinafy/golang-sdk) |
| Rust | `assinafy` | `cargo add assinafy` | [rust-sdk](https://github.com/assinafy/rust-sdk) |
| C# / .NET | `Assinafy.Sdk` | `dotnet add package Assinafy.Sdk` | [csharp-sdk](https://github.com/assinafy/csharp-sdk) |
| Java | `com.assinafy:assinafy-sdk` | GitHub Packages — see below | [java-sdk](https://github.com/assinafy/java-sdk) |
| PHP | `assinafy/php-sdk` | `composer require assinafy/php-sdk` | [php-sdk](https://github.com/assinafy/php-sdk) |

Runtime floors are current-generation: Node 22+, Python 3.10+, Ruby 3.2+, Go 1.26+, Rust 1.86+, .NET 8+, JDK 25, PHP 8.2+.

### Which Java package?

Two Java artifacts exist and they are close to identical — both ship `com.assinafy.sdk.AssinafyClient` covering the same operations. Use **java-sdk** (`com.assinafy:assinafy-sdk`) for new integrations. **webforms-java-client** (`com.assinafy:webforms-java-client-sdk`, [source](https://github.com/assinafy/webforms-java-client)) is the same client with an older setter-style options builder, kept for integrations already on it; despite the name it carries no webforms-specific API.

Neither is published to Maven Central. Both resolve from GitHub Packages at `https://maven.pkg.github.com/assinafy/{repository}`, which requires a GitHub personal access token with `read:packages` even for public artifacts.

### Which TypeScript package?

`@assinafy/sdk` is the general-purpose REST client and the right default. [`@assinafy/chat-sdk`](https://github.com/assinafy/chat-sdk) bundles that same client *plus* chat orchestration, renderable cards, adapter and state contracts, and provider-neutral AI tool definitions — reach for it only when you are building a conversational signing experience.

## Mobile SDKs

| Platform | Install | Source |
|----------|---------|--------|
| iOS / macOS | SwiftPM — add the package URL `https://github.com/assinafy/mobile-ios-sdk.git` and pin *Up to Next Major* from the current release | [mobile-ios-sdk](https://github.com/assinafy/mobile-ios-sdk) |
| Android | Gradle — `implementation("com.assinafy:assinafy-android-sdk:{version}")`, resolved from GitHub Packages (token required) | [mobile-android-sdk](https://github.com/assinafy/mobile-android-sdk) |

Both are released on GitHub Releases; take the current version from the *Releases* page of the repository rather than a number quoted here.

**Never embed an account API key in a distributed app.** A key extracted from an app bundle grants full access to the workspace. Have the app authenticate against your own back end and receive a short-lived access token, or keep account operations server-side entirely.

## Command line

[`@assinafy/cli`](https://github.com/assinafy/assinafy-cli) exposes the API as a terminal tool: readable tables by default, `--json` for scripting, and named profiles so sandbox and production credentials stay apart.

```shell
npm install -g @assinafy/cli
assinafy login
assinafy send contract.pdf --signer "Ana Lima <ana@example.com>" --message "Please sign this contract"
```

## MCP server

A Model Context Protocol server that lets an AI assistant work with documents in your workspace. It is **hosted by Assinafy — there is nothing to install or deploy**.

| | |
|---|---|
| Endpoint | `POST https://mcp.assinafy.com.br/mcp` |
| Transport | Streamable HTTP (remote) |
| Authentication | OAuth 2.0 only — API keys are not accepted |

Add it to your MCP client as a **remote HTTP** server; there is no local command to run. On first use the client opens a browser window where you sign in to Assinafy, choose a workspace and approve the requested permissions. You do not create an OAuth application or enter a client ID, client secret, API key or workspace header — the client identifies itself with a Client ID Metadata Document. For example, in Claude Code:

```shell
claude mcp add --transport http assinafy https://mcp.assinafy.com.br/mcp
claude mcp login assinafy
```

The default scopes requested are `account:read`, `documents:read`, `documents:write`, `templates:read` and `templates:write`, plus `offline_access` when the client wants a refresh token. Setup for other clients (VS Code, Codex and more) is in the [MCP server documentation](https://github.com/assinafy/mcp-server/blob/main/README.en.md).

Eleven tools are exposed:

- **Documents** — `assinafy_find_documents`, `assinafy_prepare_document`, `assinafy_download_document`, `assinafy_verify_document`, `assinafy_delete_document`
- **Signature requests** — `assinafy_request_signatures`, `assinafy_follow_up_assignment`, `assinafy_check_fields`
- **Signers** — `assinafy_find_signers`, `assinafy_save_signer`
- **Templates** — `assinafy_find_templates`

Template creation, page-layout editing, role configuration and signer-side operations (signing, verification codes, term acceptance) are deliberately not exposed to assistants. Use the REST API for those.

## n8n

[`@assinafy/n8n-nodes-assinafy`](https://github.com/assinafy/n8n-nodes-assinafy) ships three pieces: an **Assinafy** action node covering assignments, documents, fields, signers, tags, templates, webhooks and workspaces; an **Assinafy Trigger** webhook node; and a shared **Assinafy API** credential holding the API key, the account id and the environment (production, sandbox or a custom base URL).

On self-hosted n8n, open **Settings → Community Nodes** and enter `@assinafy/n8n-nodes-assinafy`, or install it in the n8n container directly:

```shell
npm install @assinafy/n8n-nodes-assinafy
```

The Trigger node derives its webhook URL authentication from the credential and can additionally verify an HMAC-SHA256 payload signature, so a subscription created from n8n needs no extra webhook setup on the Assinafy side. Availability in n8n Cloud follows n8n's own community-node review.

## In practice

```javascript
import { AssinafyClient } from '@assinafy/sdk';

const client = new AssinafyClient({
  apiKey: process.env.ASSINAFY_API_KEY,
  accountId: process.env.ASSINAFY_ACCOUNT_ID,
});

const result = await client.uploadAndRequestSignatures({
  source: { filePath: './contract.pdf' },
  signers: [{ name: 'John Dove', email: 'john@example.com' }],
  message: 'Please sign this contract',
});

console.log(result.document.id);
```

```python
import os
from assinafy import AssinafyClient

with AssinafyClient(
    api_key=os.environ['ASSINAFY_API_KEY'],
    account_id=os.environ['ASSINAFY_ACCOUNT_ID'],
) as client:
    result = client.upload_and_request_signatures(
        source={'file_path': './contract.pdf'},
        signers=[{'full_name': 'John Dove', 'email': 'john@example.com'}],
        message='Please sign this contract',
    )
    print(result['document']['id'])
```

tags.description:
This reference is generated from a single OpenAPI 3.0 document. You can download that document and load it into any OpenAPI-aware tool — Postman, Insomnia, a code generator, or your editor.

## Download the spec

The document is served at `https://api.assinafy.com.br/v1/docs/openapi.json` and always describes what is currently deployed:

```shell
curl -o assinafy-openapi.json "https://api.assinafy.com.br/v1/docs/openapi.json"
```


## Postman

There are two ways in.

**Fork the ready-made collection.** Open the [Assinafy API workspace on Postman](https://www.postman.com/assinafy/assinafy-api/overview), select the collection, then **Fork** it into your own workspace.

**Or import the spec yourself:**

1. **Import → Link**, paste `https://api.assinafy.com.br/v1/docs/openapi.json` and confirm. Postman creates a request for every operation, grouped by section.
2. On the new collection, open **Authorization**, choose **API Key**, set *Key* to `X-Api-Key`, *Value* to `{{api_key}}` and *Add to* **Header**. Every request inherits it.
3. Create an **environment** holding `base_url` (`https://sandbox.assinafy.com.br/v1` while developing) and `api_key`. Keep the key in the environment rather than the collection so it does not travel with an exported or shared collection.

## Insomnia

1. **Create → Import → From URL**, paste `https://api.assinafy.com.br/v1/docs/openapi.json`.
2. Open **Manage Environments** on the imported collection and add:

```json
{
  "base_url": "https://sandbox.assinafy.com.br/v1",
  "api_key": "your-api-key"
}
```

3. On the collection's **Headers** tab add `X-Api-Key` with value `{{ _.api_key }}` so every request inherits it.

Switching between sandbox and production is then a matter of selecting a different environment.

## Generate your own client

The document works with the usual generators:

```shell
npx @openapitools/openapi-generator-cli generate \
  -i https://api.assinafy.com.br/v1/docs/openapi.json \
  -g python \
  -o ./assinafy-client
```

Worth weighing first: the official SDKs listed under *SDKs & Tools* already unwrap the `{ status, message, data }` envelope, surface the `X-Pagination-*` response headers as pagination objects, and handle multipart document upload. A generated client hands you the raw envelope on every call and leaves that work to you.

tags.name: Authentication
tags.description:
Authentication can be done in three ways:

- API key in the `X-Api-Key` header: `X-Api-Key: {api-key}`
- Access token in the `Authorization` header: `Authorization: Bearer {access-token}`
- Access token as a URL parameter: `?access-token={access-token}`

The **recommended** method is an API key, which you create from the settings page in the Assinafy app. An access token is obtained through login with email and password; it is a JWT that usually expires in one hour.

Building an application that **other people** connect to their own workspace? Don't ask for their API key: use OAuth, which gives your app a token limited to what the user approved. See **OAuth Integration Guide**.

tags.name: OAuth Integration Guide
tags.description:
Build an application that **other people connect to their own Assinafy workspace**, without ever handling their password or API key. The user approves your app once; you receive tokens limited to the permissions they approved and to one workspace. Standard OAuth 2.1 and OpenID Connect libraries work unchanged.

### Do you need OAuth?

| | API key | OAuth |
|---|---|---|
| Acts on | **Your own** workspace | **Someone else's** workspace, with their permission |
| Can do | Everything your account can do | Only what the user approved |
| The user can switch it off | No | Yes, at any time |
| Choose it when | You automate your own account | You build an app that other people connect |

Automating your own workspace? Keep using your API key; nothing in this guide applies.

### How it works

1. Your app sends the user's browser to the authorization server, `https://auth.assinafy.com.br`.
2. The user signs in, picks **one** workspace and approves your app.
3. The browser comes back to your site with a one-time code.
4. Your server exchanges the code for tokens at `https://api.assinafy.com.br/v1/oauth/token`.
5. Your server calls this API with `Authorization: Bearer <access_token>`.

Two hosts on purpose: the browser page lives on the authorization server, and everything your code calls lives on this API.

### Create your application

You must be an **owner** of the workspace that will own the application, and the workspace's plan must include OAuth applications. In the Assinafy app (https://app.assinafy.com.br), open **Settings → OAuth applications → New application**.

| Field | What to put |
|---|---|
| Name | What users see on the approval screen |
| Description | One sentence on what the app does with their documents |
| Logo URL | Optional, an `https://` image |
| Redirect URIs | Where users return after approving, e.g. `https://myapp.com/oauth/callback`. Must be `https://`, without `#`, and is matched **exactly**: `…/callback` and `…/callback/` are different. Add one per environment you run. For local development use an https tunnel; `http://localhost` is not accepted |
| Permissions | The **most** your app will ever request. You can ask for less at connect time, never more |
| Type | **Confidential** if your code runs on a server you control; **Public** if it runs on the user's device and cannot keep a secret. Cannot be changed later |

You get a `client_id` (public) and, for Confidential apps, a `client_secret`.

> **The secret is shown once.** Store it in your server's secret storage straight away. If it is lost, rotate it: the old secret stops working immediately, so deploy the new one at once. Deleting the application disconnects every user immediately.

Building one product that **many different Assinafy customers** will connect? Talk to us first: we can register it as a verified application owned by no single workspace, with one `client_id` for every customer.

### Discovery

Most OAuth libraries only need the issuer, `https://auth.assinafy.com.br`, and read the rest from its metadata document. If you configure URLs by hand, copy them from there:

```shell
curl "https://auth.assinafy.com.br/.well-known/oauth-authorization-server"
```

```json
{
  "issuer": "https://auth.assinafy.com.br",
  "authorization_endpoint": "https://auth.assinafy.com.br/oauth/authorize",
  "token_endpoint": "https://api.assinafy.com.br/v1/oauth/token",
  "revocation_endpoint": "https://api.assinafy.com.br/v1/oauth/revoke",
  "userinfo_endpoint": "https://api.assinafy.com.br/v1/oauth/userinfo",
  "jwks_uri": "https://auth.assinafy.com.br/.well-known/jwks.json",
  "response_types_supported": ["code"],
  "grant_types_supported": ["authorization_code", "refresh_token"],
  "code_challenge_methods_supported": ["S256"],
  "token_endpoint_auth_methods_supported": ["client_secret_post", "none"]
}
```

The metadata and key documents are served **only** by the authorization server. This API serves its own protected-resource metadata at `https://api.assinafy.com.br/.well-known/oauth-protected-resource`.

### Connect a user

#### 1. Create a PKCE pair and a state

PKCE is required for **every** application, Confidential ones included. Create a new pair for each connection attempt:

```js
import crypto from 'node:crypto';

const b64url = (buf) => buf.toString('base64url');

const codeVerifier  = b64url(crypto.randomBytes(32));
const codeChallenge = b64url(crypto.createHash('sha256').update(codeVerifier).digest());
const state         = b64url(crypto.randomBytes(16));

// Keep codeVerifier and state in the user's session: step 3 and 4 need them.
```

The verifier must be 43 to 128 characters from `A-Z a-z 0-9 - . _ ~`.

#### 2. Send the browser to the authorization server

Use a full page navigation (a link or a redirect), not an AJAX call. Shown unencoded for readability; URL-encode every value:

```
https://auth.assinafy.com.br/oauth/authorize
  ?response_type=code
  &client_id=YOUR_CLIENT_ID
  &redirect_uri=https://myapp.com/oauth/callback
  &scope=documents:read documents:write offline_access
  &state=STATE
  &code_challenge=CODE_CHALLENGE
  &code_challenge_method=S256
  &resource=https://api.assinafy.com.br
```

| Parameter | Notes |
|---|---|
| `redirect_uri` | One of your registered URIs, character for character |
| `scope` | Space-separated, within what the application is registered for |
| `state` | Random per attempt; your CSRF protection |
| `code_challenge_method` | Only `S256` |
| `resource` | `https://api.assinafy.com.br`, naming the API the token is for. Recommended |
| `nonce` | Optional, echoed in the `id_token` when you request `openid` |

If the `client_id` or `redirect_uri` is wrong, the user is **not** sent back to you: the authorization server shows an error on its own page, because redirecting to an unverified address would be unsafe. Users reporting that they are stuck on an Assinafy error page usually means one of those two values is wrong.

#### 3. Handle the return

Approved:

```
https://myapp.com/oauth/callback?code=…&state=…&iss=https://auth.assinafy.com.br
```

Declined or invalid:

```
https://myapp.com/oauth/callback?error=access_denied&error_description=…&state=…&iss=https://auth.assinafy.com.br
```

Before anything else, check that `state` equals what you stored and that `iss` equals `https://auth.assinafy.com.br`. If either differs, stop: the response is not yours.

#### 4. Exchange the code for tokens

From your server. The code is single-use and expires **60 seconds** after approval.

```shell
curl -X POST "https://api.assinafy.com.br/v1/oauth/token" \
  -H 'Content-Type: application/x-www-form-urlencoded' \
  -d grant_type=authorization_code \
  -d code=THE_CODE \
  -d redirect_uri=https://myapp.com/oauth/callback \
  -d client_id=YOUR_CLIENT_ID \
  -d client_secret=YOUR_CLIENT_SECRET \
  -d code_verifier=THE_CODE_VERIFIER \
  -d resource=https://api.assinafy.com.br
```

Public applications send the same request without `client_secret`.

```json
{
  "access_token": "…",
  "token_type": "Bearer",
  "expires_in": 3600,
  "scope": "documents:read documents:write",
  "refresh_token": "…",
  "id_token": "…"
}
```

- `refresh_token` is present only when you requested `offline_access`; `id_token` only when you requested `openid`. `offline_access` itself never appears in `scope`: it only asks for a refresh token and isn't a permission the access token carries.
- `scope` is what you **actually** received. Read it instead of assuming.
- OAuth token responses are plain JSON objects, not wrapped in the `{ status, message, data }` envelope the rest of this API uses.

#### 5. Find the workspace, then call the API

A token belongs to the one workspace the user picked. With an OAuth token, the workspace list returns exactly that workspace:

```shell
curl "https://api.assinafy.com.br/v1/accounts" \
  -H 'Authorization: Bearer ACCESS_TOKEN'
```

Store `data[0].id` next to the tokens, then call the API:

```shell
curl "https://api.assinafy.com.br/v1/accounts/WORKSPACE_ID/documents" \
  -H 'Authorization: Bearer ACCESS_TOKEN'
```

Always send the token in the `Authorization: Bearer` header. A token sent as `X-Api-Key` or in the query string is refused.

### Permissions (scopes)

| Scope | Lets your app |
|---|---|
| `documents:read` | Read documents, their signers, assignments and activity, the WhatsApp notifications sent for an assignment, and webhook event types and delivery history |
| `documents:write` | Create documents and send them for signature |
| `templates:read` | Read templates |
| `templates:write` | Create and change templates |
| `account:read` | Read the workspace's profile, theme and logo, its document KPIs (stats), and its webhook subscription and endpoints |
| `webhooks:write` | Change where and which webhook events are delivered, deactivate the webhook subscription, manage webhook endpoints, get a new signing secret for one (by turning signing on or rotating it), and re-send a delivery (**Retry Webhook Dispatch**) |
| `openid` | Receive an `id_token` identifying the user |
| `profile` | Read the user's name |
| `email` | Read the user's email and whether it is verified |
| `offline_access` | Receive a refresh token, to keep working while the user is away |

- Request the minimum. Every permission is another line the user reads before deciding.
- `documents:write` can spend the workspace's notification credits, since sending for signature notifies signers.
- The user approves everything you requested, or nothing. If a feature needs more later, run the flow again requesting the larger set.
- Billing and subscriptions, workspace membership, credentials and administration are **never** available to an OAuth token, whatever its scopes.

Calling an endpoint without the scope it requires returns `403` with a challenge naming the missing scope:

```
WWW-Authenticate: Bearer error="insufficient_scope", scope="documents:write", resource_metadata="https://api.assinafy.com.br/.well-known/oauth-protected-resource"
```

Treat it as a prompt to reconnect with that scope added, not as a request to retry. A `403` without this header has another cause: a different workspace, the user's own role, or an area OAuth tokens can never reach.

### Resource indicators

`resource` (RFC 8707) names **which service** a token is for. Omit it and you get a token for
this API — that is what every direct integration wants, and nothing about it has changed.

Assinafy also runs a separate MCP server, which is its own protected resource. A token minted
for it authenticates against *that* server and is refused here, and the reverse is also true.
If you are calling this API directly, send `https://api.assinafy.com.br` or omit the parameter.

A refresh may repeat the original `resource` but never change it; a different value is
rejected with `invalid_target`.

> **Operator note.** The confidential client backing Assinafy's own MCP server is an
> **internal-service client** (`is_internal_service`), provisioned outside this
> self-serve flow. It has no `redirect_uris` and cannot pass through the ordinary
> secret-rotation endpoint — that write requires `redirect_uris` under the client's
> default validation scenario, which an internal-service client deliberately has none
> of. If its secret leaks, the recovery path is **disable the client and provision a
> new one**, then reconfigure the MCP server with the new credentials — not "rotate the
> secret."

### One connection, one workspace

The integration mistake we see most often. A token works only for the workspace the user chose; calling any other workspace returns `403`, even one the same user belongs to. If your customer uses several workspaces, connect each one separately and keep tokens per workspace.

### Refresh tokens

Access tokens last **1 hour**. With `offline_access`, renew them without the user:

```shell
curl -X POST "https://api.assinafy.com.br/v1/oauth/token" \
  -H 'Content-Type: application/x-www-form-urlencoded' \
  -d grant_type=refresh_token \
  -d refresh_token=CURRENT_REFRESH_TOKEN \
  -d client_id=YOUR_CLIENT_ID \
  -d client_secret=YOUR_CLIENT_SECRET
```

Every refresh returns a **new** refresh token and retires the old one.

> **Using an old refresh token disconnects the user.** A reused refresh token cannot be told apart from a stolen one being replayed, so it ends the whole connection: every token stops working and the user must connect again.
>
> 1. Save the new refresh token before doing anything else with the response.
> 2. Treat a timeout as "maybe it worked": re-read your saved token before retrying, never retry blindly with the old one.
> 3. Refresh one at a time per connection.

- A refresh token is valid for **30 days**, and every refresh returns a new one with a fresh 30 days. A connection only expires if your app goes 30 days without refreshing; after that, the user has to reconnect.
- If the user approves your app again with different permissions, the previous tokens stop working immediately.

### Disconnecting

When a user disconnects in your product, revoke the token instead of only deleting it. The endpoint always answers `200`:

```shell
curl -X POST "https://api.assinafy.com.br/v1/oauth/revoke" \
  -d token=THE_REFRESH_OR_ACCESS_TOKEN \
  -d client_id=YOUR_CLIENT_ID \
  -d client_secret=YOUR_CLIENT_SECRET
```

Users can also revoke your app themselves under **Connected apps** in their Assinafy profile. Deleting or disabling your application has the same effect. In every case your tokens stop working at once: handle the `401` by asking the user to connect again.

> **Revoking a token requires the `client_id` that owns it.** `/oauth/revoke` only revokes a token issued to the client authenticating the call. This matters for an RFC 8693 exchanged token specifically: it carries the *original* (front-end resource) client's id, not the service client that exchanged it — so a back-channel service client can never revoke a token it derived, and the call still answers `200` per RFC 7009's always-succeed contract, giving no indication that nothing happened. That derived token is inherently short-lived (bounded by the exchanged-token TTL), so it ages out on its own; do not build a cleanup call expecting revoke to work on it.

### Verification and limits

- New applications are **unverified**: the approval screen warns that Assinafy has not reviewed the app, and it can be connected to at most **25 workspaces**. Before launching beyond a pilot, ask us to verify it, telling us what the app does and why it needs each permission.
- The authorize and token endpoints accept **50 requests per minute per IP**. Normal traffic stays far below that; hitting it usually means a refresh loop.
- Applications are created in the Assinafy app, not through an API.

### Errors

On your redirect URI (`?error=…`):

| `error` | Meaning |
|---|---|
| `access_denied` | The user declined |
| `invalid_scope` | A scope your application is not registered for, or none |
| `invalid_request` | Missing or malformed PKCE parameters |
| `unsupported_response_type` | Anything other than `response_type=code` |
| `invalid_target` | A `resource` other than `https://api.assinafy.com.br` |

From the token endpoint (`{ "error": "…", "error_description": "…" }`):

| `error` | Usual causes |
|---|---|
| `invalid_grant` | Code expired or already used, wrong `code_verifier` or `redirect_uri`; refresh token already used or expired, or the user reconnected with different permissions |
| `invalid_client` | Wrong `client_id` or secret, or the application is disabled |
| `invalid_target` | `resource` does not match what was authorized |
| `unsupported_grant_type` | Only `authorization_code` and `refresh_token` exist |

From API calls:

| Status | Meaning |
|---|---|
| `401` | Token expired, revoked, or not sent as `Bearer`. Refresh; if that fails, ask the user to reconnect |
| `403` with `insufficient_scope` | Missing permission. Reconnect requesting the scope in `WWW-Authenticate` |
| `403` otherwise | Another workspace, or an area OAuth tokens cannot reach |
| `429` | Too many requests. Back off and retry later |

### Signing users in (OpenID Connect)

Request `openid`, plus `profile` and/or `email`, to receive an `id_token`: a signed JWT saying who approved. Validate it with any OpenID Connect library:

- signature `RS256`, keys at `https://auth.assinafy.com.br/.well-known/jwks.json` (match the `kid`);
- `iss` equals `https://auth.assinafy.com.br`;
- `aud` equals your `client_id`;
- `exp` is in the future, and `nonce` matches the one you sent, if any.

`sub` is the user's stable identifier. For their name and email, call **OpenID Connect userinfo** (`GET https://api.assinafy.com.br/v1/oauth/userinfo`).

### AI assistants

Claude, Claude Code and ChatGPT connect to Assinafy on their own through their connector settings. Your users do not need you to build or register anything for them.

### Before you go live

- A new PKCE verifier and `state` for every connection attempt
- `state` and `iss` checked on your redirect URI
- `client_secret` only on your server, never in a mobile app, browser code or a repository
- The new refresh token saved before use, and one refresh at a time per connection
- `401` handled: refresh, and if that fails, ask the user to reconnect
- The workspace id stored per connection, and the returned `scope` read
- Every production redirect URI registered, `https://` and exact
- Only the permissions you need
- Tokens revoked when a user disconnects
- Verification requested
