tags.name: Contracts
tags.description:
Contract terms tracked on documents: counterparty, value, dates and renewal terms. A contract always belongs to a document of the workspace, and tracking it never changes how that document is uploaded, sent or signed.

### How the flow works

1. **Have the document first.** Upload it with `POST /v1/accounts/{accountId}/documents`, or pick one already in the workspace, and keep its `id`. No call creates a document and its contract terms together.
2. **Set its terms.** `PUT /v1/accounts/{accountId}/documents/{documentId}/contract` with the terms. Any time: right after the upload, while the document is out for signature, or long after it was signed. A contract that ended before it was tracked is registered as it ended (`expired` with a past `end_date`, or `terminated`). A cancelled, declined or expired document takes no new terms. If this call fails, the document stays uploaded and the terms can be sent again.
3. **Record a change with a signed instrument** (optional). Upload the amendment, renewal or termination document, then `PUT` its own `.../contract` with `parent_document_id` (the contract's document), `relation_type` and the terms it changes. The change applies to the contract once that document is signed (at once if it already is), and `document_contract_amended` is recorded.
4. **Let the hourly run keep it current.** Every active contract is walked by the Brasília calendar day: the renewal notice when the notice period starts, warnings 45 and 30 days before the end date, and, the day after it, the next term for an auto-renew contract or `expired` for the others. Each records its `document_contract_*` event and e-mails the contract's owner. The same run hands the contracts of an owner who left the workspace, however they left, to the first owner still an active member.
5. **Or change it directly.** `PUT` edits the terms, `POST .../renew` starts the next term and `POST .../terminate` closes the contract.
6. **Read it.** `GET /v1/accounts/{accountId}/contracts` lists the workspace's contracts; `GET .../documents/{documentId}/contract` reads one with its amendments; `GET /v1/documents/{documentId}` says whether a document has one (`has_contract`). Every change is an event on the document's activities and a webhook.

### Who can write

Writes need a plan with contract tracking; reads do not. Any active member of the workspace, owner or organizer, may set terms, link amendments, renew and terminate; an OAuth app needs `documents:write` to write and `documents:read` to read.

### Errors and conflicts

A refused write lists every problem in `errors`, each with its `field` and a stable `code`; the codes and the rules behind them are in the `400` response. A write that sends the `updated_at` it read is refused with `409` if the contract changed meanwhile.

### When the plan lapses

While the workspace's plan lacks contract tracking (its subscription expired or was cancelled; a payment past due inside the grace period keeps it), the hourly run leaves its contracts as they are and signed amendments wait. The first run after the plan returns catches up: a contract past its end date moves to the term running that day, on its own renewal cycle, or expires; waiting amendments apply in signing order; alerts whose window passed meanwhile are not sent.

tags.name: Verification & Notification Methods
tags.description:
When you create an assignment, each signer can be configured with a **verification method** (how the signer proves their identity before signing) and a **notification method** (how the signer is told a signature is being requested). Exactly one notification method is allowed per signer; `notification_methods` is an array for historical reasons, and sending more than one entry returns `400`. These are set per signer via `signers[].verification_method` and `signers[].notification_methods` on the **Create assignment** endpoint.

Verification and notification are **coupled** — you may send one, both or neither, and the missing side is inferred. If neither is sent, both default to `Email`.

### Verification methods

| Code | Description |
|------|-------------|
| `Email` | The signer receives a verification code by email that must be entered before signing. |
| `Whatsapp` | The signer receives a verification code over WhatsApp that must be entered before signing. Requires the WhatsApp notification channel — the two always travel together. |
| `DigitalCertificate` | The signer signs with their own ICP-Brasil digital certificate (A1/A3) from their device using the Web PKI browser extension, producing a qualified PAdES signature on the document. **Only on `virtual` assignments**: the certificate flow does not fill placed fields, so it can't be combined with them (`collect`, or a template with placed signer fields). |
| `IdDocumentFaceMatchBasic` | Identity document verification. Before seeing the document, the signer consents, photographs an identity document, takes a photo holding it and passes a liveness check; the result must match the CPF and name you registered for the signer. See **Identity document verification** below. |

| Code | Requirements | Cost per signer (verification + its notification) |
|------|--------------|---------------------------------------------------|
| `Email` | Signer must have an email address. | 0 credits (the Email notification) |
| `Whatsapp` | Signer must have a `whatsapp_phone_number`; available only on paid subscriptions. | 0.45 credits (the WhatsApp notification, which this method requires) |
| `DigitalCertificate` | Account must have the **Digital Certificate** feature (Standard and Pro plans). Signer must have a CPF in `government_id`. Each digital-certificate signer must be **alone in its signing step**, and the assignment must be `virtual` (no placed fields); a `collect` assignment, or a template with placed signer fields, returns `400`. | 0.5 credits + its notification |
| `IdDocumentFaceMatchBasic` | Account must have the **identity document verification** feature, enabled on request. Signer must have a full name and a valid CPF in `government_id` (a CNPJ is refused). | Your plan's verification price (see below) + its notification |

> **How verification is priced.** `Email`, `Whatsapp` and `DigitalCertificate` verification carry no price of their own — you are billed for the **notification** they are paired with (plus, for `DigitalCertificate`, the signature itself). Because verification and notification are coupled, choosing `Whatsapp` verification also chooses the WhatsApp notification, so a WhatsApp-verified signer costs 0.45 credits against 0 credits for an email-verified one. The column above is that combined per-signer cost, which is what the **Estimate assignment cost** endpoint returns.

> **Digital Certificate cost.** Unlike `Email` and `Whatsapp` verification (whose only cost is the notification), the digital-certificate signature itself is charged **0.5 credits per digital-certificate signer**, on top of the notification cost. The charge is applied when the assignment is created, and appears in the **Estimate assignment cost** breakdown under the `SignatureDigitalCertificate` code.

> **Identity document verification cost.** `IdDocumentFaceMatchBasic` is charged per signer, on top of the notification cost, at a price that depends on your plan (below). The charge is applied when the assignment is created, and appears in the **Estimate assignment cost** breakdown under the `VerificationIdDocumentFaceMatchBasic` code.

| Plan | Price per signer |
|------|------------------|
| Free | 1.5 credits |
| Standard | 1 credit |
| Pro | 0.5 credits |
| Other plans and enterprise contracts | 0.25 credits |

### Notification methods

The notification method is what delivers the signing invitation to the signer. Each notification has a credit cost charged when the assignment is created (and again when a notification is resent).

| Code | Description |
|------|-------------|
| `Email` | Sends an email invitation with a link to sign the document. |
| `Whatsapp` | Sends a WhatsApp message with a link to sign the document. |

| Code | Requirements | Cost (per signer) |
|------|--------------|-------------------|
| `Email` | Signer must have an email address. | 0 credits |
| `Whatsapp` | Signer must have a `whatsapp_phone_number`; available only on paid subscriptions. | 0.45 credits |

### Coupling rules

Only matching combinations are allowed; an invalid pairing returns `400 Bad Request`.

| Verification method | Allowed notification methods |
|---------------------|------------------------------|
| `Email` | `Email` |
| `Whatsapp` | `Whatsapp` |
| `DigitalCertificate` | `Email` or `Whatsapp` |
| `IdDocumentFaceMatchBasic` | `Email` or `Whatsapp` (inferred: `Email`) |

Exactly one notification method is allowed per signer — `notification_methods` takes a single-element array, and a second entry is rejected with `400` before the pairing above is even checked.

### Default behavior (inference)

- **Neither specified** — both default to `Email`.
- **Only `verification_method`** — `notification_methods` is inferred from it (e.g. `Whatsapp` verification → `Whatsapp` notification, and with it that channel's cost).
- **Only `notification_methods`** — `verification_method` is inferred from it.
- **Both specified** — used as-is, subject to the coupling rules above.

### Costs

Notification cost is charged **per signer**, on top of the document cost. For example:

- 2 signers notified by email = 0 credits
- 2 signers notified by WhatsApp = 0.9 credits

Verification follows the same arithmetic, because it is the notification that is billed: 2 signers **verified** by WhatsApp are necessarily notified by WhatsApp, and therefore also cost 0.9 credits. The exceptions are `DigitalCertificate` and `IdDocumentFaceMatchBasic`, which add their own per-signer charge on top of the notification.

Use the **Estimate assignment cost** endpoint to preview the exact total (documents + notifications + verification and signature charges) before creating an assignment.

### Notification timing and sequential signing

By default every signer is notified as soon as the assignment is created. When you set `signers[].step` to define a signing order, each signer's notification is held until their step is activated: step 1 is notified at creation, and a later step is notified only after every signer in the previous step has finished.

### Identity document verification

With `IdDocumentFaceMatchBasic`, identity verification is the signer's first step:

1. The signer opens the invitation and gives consent (**Start identity document verification**). The response carries the capture `url`, which the signer opens on their phone to photograph the document, take a photo holding it and pass the liveness check.
2. Back on the signing page, **Identity document verification status** reports the result. The document's signer list also shows it in `identity_verification_status`.

| Result | What happens |
|--------|--------------|
| `Approved` | The document, CPF and name matched. The signer views and signs normally. |
| `InReview` | The service could not decide (for instance, the name differs slightly from the document). The signer **still views and signs**; the account is emailed to review. Once every signer has signed, the document waits in `pending_identity_review` instead of being certificated. |
| `Declined` | The verification failed. The signer cannot sign this document. |
| `Expired` | The capture link lapsed before anything was submitted; the signer may start again. |
| `Abandoned` | The signer left the capture unfinished. As with `Declined`, they cannot restart; send a new document to verify them again. |

**Reviewing.** A user of the account opens the review with **Signer identity review** (reasons, expected vs. read data, checks and evidence images, each fetched with **Signer identity review image** while the review is open), then decides with **Decide signer identity review**:

- **Approved** — the document is certificated once every signer has signed and no other review is pending.
- **Rejected** — the document is cancelled (`rejected_by_user`, with the reviewer as the user) and every signer receives the usual cancellation notice. The reviewer's note is never shown to signers.

An unreviewed document still expires at its deadline, and deleting a `pending_identity_review` document cancels it and notifies the signers. A signer under review in a sequential flow completes their step, so the next step is notified right away.

Each step of the process is recorded as a `signer_identity_*` activity and webhook event (see the **Event catalog**). A verification belongs to one document and is never reused for another.

tags.name: Webhook Payloads
tags.description:
This section documents the HTTP request your endpoint receives whenever a subscribed event is triggered, and the shape of the JSON body sent for each event type.

### Delivery contract

When an event occurs, we send an HTTP `POST` request to every active webhook endpoint subscribed to that event. Each endpoint is delivered to independently: a slow or failing endpoint does not delay the others, and each has its own failure count.

| Property | Value |
|----------|-------|
| Method | `POST` |
| Content-Type | `application/json` |
| Connection header | `close` |
| `webhook-id` header | Message ID, identical on every attempt of the same event to the same endpoint. Use it to deduplicate. |
| `webhook-timestamp` header | Unix timestamp (seconds) of the attempt. |
| `webhook-signature` header | Only when signing is enabled on the endpoint. See **Verifying signatures**. |
| Success criteria | Any `2xx` response |
| `User-Agent` header | `Assinafy-Webhooks/1.0` |
| Attempts | Up to 6 per event, about 10 minutes apart. A connection error, a timeout, a `408`, a `429` or a `5xx` is retried; any other status is final. |
| Pause | After 10 failed deliveries in a row the endpoint is paused (`is_held` on the endpoint): nothing is sent to it, and we probe it with the oldest event it missed after 3 minutes, then 15, then 60, then every 6 hours. The probe that gets through lifts the pause and the events it missed are delivered oldest first. Editing the endpoint's URL, or sending `is_active: true`, lifts the pause too. |
| Retry endpoint | **Retry webhook delivery** sends one delivery now, even while the endpoint is paused; a delivery that gets through lifts the pause. |
| Response capture | We store the first 2000 characters of your response body for debugging (see **List webhook deliveries**). Delivery entries are kept for 7 days. |

Your endpoint must respond within a reasonable time and return a `2xx` status. Non-`2xx` responses, connection errors and timeouts are all failed deliveries and count toward the pause; each delivery entry says whether another attempt follows (`will_retry`).

### Verifying signatures

Enable signing on an endpoint (`signing_enabled: true`) and every delivery carries a signature that proves it came from us and was not altered or replayed. Signatures follow the [Standard Webhooks](https://www.standardwebhooks.com) specification, so any Standard Webhooks library can verify them; the secret is returned once, as `secret`, in the **Create webhook endpoint** response, and can be read again with **Get webhook endpoint signing secret**. OAuth applications cannot call that endpoint: store the secret from the create response, and if it is lost, get a new one with **Rotate webhook endpoint signing secret**. Turning signing on with **Update webhook endpoint** also returns the new secret once.

To verify by hand:

1. Take the **raw** request body, exactly as received (do not re-serialize the parsed JSON).
2. Build the signed content `{webhook-id}.{webhook-timestamp}.{body}`.
3. Base64-decode the part of the secret after the `whsec_` prefix and compute the HMAC-SHA256 of the signed content with it. Base64-encode the result.
4. `webhook-signature` holds one or more space-separated `v1,<signature>` entries; accept the request if any of them equals your value (use a constant-time comparison).
5. Reject requests whose `webhook-timestamp` is more than a few minutes away from your clock, to prevent replays.

```php
$secret = base64_decode(substr($endpointSecret, strlen('whsec_')));
$signedContent = $headers['webhook-id'] . '.' . $headers['webhook-timestamp'] . '.' . $rawBody;
$expected = 'v1,' . base64_encode(hash_hmac('sha256', $signedContent, $secret, true));

$valid = false;
foreach (explode(' ', $headers['webhook-signature']) as $signature) {
    $valid = $valid || hash_equals($expected, $signature);
}
$fresh = abs(time() - (int) $headers['webhook-timestamp']) <= 300;
```

Rotating the secret (**Rotate webhook endpoint signing secret**) takes effect immediately: deliveries sent after the rotation are signed only with the new secret.

### Common envelope

Every webhook body shares the same top-level structure:

| Field | Type | Description |
|-------|------|-------------|
| `id` | integer | Internal activity ID that produced this event. To deduplicate retries, prefer the `webhook-id` header, which also tells deliveries of the same event to different endpoints apart. |
| `event` | string | Event type identifier. See the catalog below and the **List webhook event types** endpoint. |
| `message` | string \\| null | Human-readable message describing the event. May contain token placeholders. Can be `null`. |
| `payload` | object \\| null | Event-specific parameters. Keys vary per event — see the catalog. Can be `null`. |
| `origin` | object \\| null | Where the action was triggered from, when available: `{ ip, user-agent }`. |
| `created_at` | integer | Unix timestamp (seconds) when the event was recorded. |
| `subject` | object | The entity that performed the action. Polymorphic — see below. |
| `object` | object | The entity the action was performed on. Polymorphic — see below. |
| `account_id` | string | The ID of the account that owns this event. Always present. |

### About `subject` and `object`

Both are **polymorphic**: their shape depends on which entity they represent. We always add a `type` property with the entity class name, one of `User`, `Signer`, `Account`, `Document`, or `Template`. The remaining properties match the same fields the REST API returns for that resource. The `object` is serialized with its extra relationships expanded (e.g. a `Document` includes `assignment` and `pages`); the `subject` carries its base fields only. Whenever `subject` or `object` is an `Account`, the `integration` property (which includes dispatch history) is removed before sending.

For `document_ready`, `document_processing_failed` and `template_processing_failed`, the `subject` is the `Account` itself — these events are emitted by the system when processing finishes, not by a particular user.

### Event catalog

Each event also has its own entry under **Webhooks** with a complete example body.

| Event | Subject | Object | `payload` keys | Description |
|-------|---------|--------|----------------|-------------|
| `document_uploaded` | User | Document | — | The user uploaded a new document. |
| `document_metadata_ready` | User | Document | — | The document was normalized to PDF and its pages are available. |
| `document_prepared` | User | Document | — | The user prepared a document (fields assigned to signers). |
| `assignment_created` | User | Document | `user_name`, `user_email`, `user_telephone` | The user created an assignment for the document. Includes a snapshot of the creator profile. |
| `document_ready` | Account | Document | — | The document was certificated after every signer signed (and, when a signer's identity was under review, after the account approved it). |
| `document_processing_failed` | Account | Document | `error_message` | The document could not be processed. |
| `signature_requested` | User | Document | `signer_full_name`, `signer_email`, `signer_whatsapp_phone_number`, `notification_method` | The user requested a signer to sign the document. |
| `signer_created` | User | Signer | `signer_full_name` | The user created a new signer. |
| `signer_email_verified` | Signer | Document | `signer_full_name`, `signer_email` | The signer's email was verified through a code linked to the document. |
| `signer_whatsapp_verified` | Signer | Document | `signer_full_name`, `signer_whatsapp_phone_number` | The signer's WhatsApp number was verified through a code linked to the document. |
| `signer_data_confirmed` | Signer | Document | `signer_full_name`, `signer_email`, `signer_whatsapp_phone_number`, `verification_method` | The signer confirmed their data before signing. |
| `signer_viewed_document` | Signer | Document | `signer_full_name` | The signer opened the document for the first time. |
| `signer_identity_verified` | Signer | Document | `signer_full_name`, `evidence` (when available) | The signer passed identity-document verification, directly or after the account's review. |
| `signer_identity_verification_failed` | Signer | Document | `signer_full_name`, `reason` | The identity-document verification ended without approval. |
| `signer_identity_review_required` | Signer | Document | `signer_full_name`, `reason_codes` | The verification awaits the account's review. The signer can still sign; the document is certificated only after the account approves (status `pending_identity_review` once every signer has signed). |
| `signer_identity_review_approved` | Signer | Document | `signer_full_name`, `reviewer_id`, `reviewer_name`, `reason_codes` | A user of the account approved the signer's identity after review. |
| `signer_identity_review_rejected` | Signer | Document | `signer_full_name`, `reviewer_id`, `reviewer_name`, `note` | A user of the account rejected the signer's identity after review. The document is cancelled; `user_rejected_document` follows. |
| `signer_signed_document` | Signer | Document | `signer_full_name` | The signer signed the document. |
| `signer_rejected_document` | Signer | Document | `signer_full_name` | The signer refused to sign the document. |
| `user_rejected_document` | User | Document | `user_name` | The document was cancelled by a user of the account. |
| `template_created` | User | Template | — | The user created a new template. |
| `template_processed` | User | Template | — | A template's metadata was processed and is ready for use. |
| `template_processing_failed` | Account | Template | `error_message` | A template could not be processed. |

`assignment_created` and `document_metadata_ready` have no guaranteed ordering: under the virtual pre-metadata flow, `assignment_created` may fire before `document_metadata_ready`. Treat any unknown field as a forward-compatible addition.
